name: Roc Retin-Ox

lead: Retin-Ox is a retinol-based product name from RoC, the skincare brand founded in Paris in 1957 by pharmacist Jean-Charles Lissarrague. RoC says it was the first to formulate stabilised retinol, which Wikipedia dates to 1996, and retinol anti-aging products are its best-known line.

Retinol is converted by the skin into retinal and then retinoic acid, the active forms, and is used to reduce fine wrinkles and rough skin texture. Improvements are reported not to be maintained once use stops.

paras: Retinol products are used as part of a skincare routine, typically in the evening, alongside moisturiser and daytime sunscreen. Results accumulate over weeks of regular use.

A common effect is retinoid dermatitis, with redness, scaling, dryness and itching. High doses of preformed vitamin A in early pregnancy are linked to birth defects. In the US retinol is sold over the counter; EU and UK rules from November 2025 cap concentrations and require labelling.

angle.text: Retinol is a standard cosmetic ingredient for visible aging and rough texture. Users apply it in their routine for gradual smoothing.

lead: RoC is a skincare brand founded in Paris in 1957 by French pharmacist Jean-Charles Lissarrague, launched with fragrance-free products for sensitive skin and a broad-spectrum sunscreen. It is now headquartered in New York and has changed owners several times, including Dior, Johnson & Johnson (1993) and Gryphon Investors (2019), with Bridgepoint agreeing to acquire it in 2024.[1]

The brand says it was the first to formulate stabilised retinol, which the article dates to 1996, and it is known for retinol anti-aging creams, eye creams and sunscreens. Retin-Ox is one of its retinol product names.[1]

Topical retinol is converted by the body to retinal and then retinoic acid, and is used to reduce wrinkles and other signs of skin aging; clinical studies have looked at fine wrinkles and roughness on the face and neck.[2]

paras: RoC was founded by Jean-Charles Lissarrague in 1957, and Parfums Christian Dior bought it in 1978 before Johnson & Johnson acquired it in 1993.[1] The brand says it pioneered stabilised retinol in 1996.[1]

After application, retinol is converted to retinal and then retinoic acid. Studies have examined effects on fine wrinkles and roughness, with the improvement reported as not maintained after application is discontinued.[2]

In the US, all-trans retinol has been used in OTC cosmetics since 1984. In the EU and UK, rules effective November 2025 cap retinol at 0.05% retinol equivalent in body lotion and 0.3% in other products, with mandatory labelling.[2]

A common side effect is retinoid dermatitis with redness, scaling, dryness and itching.[2] High doses of preformed vitamin A during early pregnancy are linked to birth defects, and the FDA advises obtaining vitamin A from beta-carotene foods rather than exceeding 5,000 IU of preformed vitamin A daily.[2]
No studies found for this specific product. Studies of topical retinol as a category are described in the retinol article.[2]
